title: Theorem
body_md:
Let ${\mathcal Q}_0$ be a rational curve in ${\mathds P}^2$ which determines a certain Noether-Lefschetz divisor as in Secton \ref{mainconstruction}. Let $A$ be an Abelian surface whose moduli point does not lie on that divisor.  Let ${\mathcal Z}_{{\mathcal Q}_0,P,R}$ be the cycle in $H^3_{{\mathcal M}}(A,{\mathds Q}(2))$ determined by ${\mathcal Q}_0$, a node $P$  and an auxilliary point $R$ as in Theorem \ref{construction}. Then there is a hyperellipic curve ${\tilde{D}}$ mapping to a curve $D$ on $A$ and points $P_1,P_2$ and $\tilde{R}$ on ${\tilde{D}}$ such that under the induced map from the Jacobian 
$\pi:J({\tilde{D}})\rightarrow A$
	 
	$$\pi_*(Z_{P_1,P_2,\tilde{R}})=2 {\mathcal Z}_{{\mathcal Q}_0,P,R}$$
	 
	where $Z_{P_1,P_2,\tilde{R}}$ is the cycle constructed by Collino in $CH^{g}(J({\tilde{D}}),1)=H^{2g-1}_{{\mathcal M}}(J({\tilde{D}}),{\mathds Z}(g))$  as in section \ref{collino}.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Suppose $C$ is a {\bf nodal rational}  curve on a surface $X$ with node $P$. Let $\pi:\tilde{X}\rightarrow X$ denote the blow up of $X$ at $P$ such that the strict transform $\tilde{C}$ of $C$ no longer has a node at $P$. Let $P_1$ and $P_2$ be the two points lying over $P$ on $\tilde{C}$.  If $E_P$ is the exceptional fibre it is a rational curve and it meets the strict transform at the points $P_1$ and $P_2$. Let $f$ be a function with $\operatorname{div}(f)=P_1-P_2$ on $\tilde{C}$ and let $g$ be a function on $E_P$ with divisor $\operatorname{div} (g)=P_2-P_1$. Then
	 
	 $$\pi_*((\tilde{C},f)+(E_P,g))$$
	  
	  is a cycle in $H^{3}_{{\mathcal M}}(X,{\mathds Z}(2))$.
	
	\label{construction}

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $A$ be an Abelian surface and ${\mathds P}^2_A$ the corresponding configulation of ${\mathds P}^2$ with six lines $l_i$ tangent to a conic. Let $q_{ij}=l_i \cap l_j$ denote the fifteen nodal points of the degenerate sextic $S_A$. Then $A$ corresponds to a point on $H_{5}$ if and only if there exist a conic ${\mathcal Q}$ passing through five of the points $q_{ij}$ and tangent to the remaining line.
head: environment

label: rationalcurve
title: Proposition
body_md:
Let ${\mathcal Q}$ be a rational curve on ${\mathds P}^2_A$ which meets the sextic $S_A$ only at points of even multiplicity or at the double points $q_{ij}$ as in the theorems of Birkenhake and Wilhelm. Let $\psi:{\mathcal C} \longrightarrow Q$ be the double cover. Then ${\mathcal C}$ is {\bf not} irreducible and is the union of two rational curves ${\mathcal C}_1$ and ${\mathcal C}_2$. 
	
	\label{rationalcurve}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The map ${\mathcal C} \longrightarrow {\mathcal Q}$ is ramified at the points of ${\mathcal Q} \cap S_A$ which are all double points. Hence the ramification points are nodes of ${\mathcal C}$. Let $\psi:\tilde{{\mathcal C}} \longrightarrow \tilde{{\mathcal Q}}$ be the maps between the normalizations induced by $\psi$. As all the ramification points of ${\mathcal C} \rightarrow {\mathcal Q}$ are singular points,  $\tilde{{\mathcal C}}$  is an {\bf unramified} double cover of a ${\mathds P}^1$. Since the fundamental group of ${\mathds P}^1$ is trivial, there are no {\bf irreducible} unramified double covers.  Hence $\tilde{{\mathcal C}}$ is the union of two rational curves meeting at a point and ${\mathcal C}$ is the union of two curves ${\mathcal C}_1$ and ${\mathcal C}_2$ which meet at the points lying over the ramification points.

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $n_d$ be the number of {\em rational} curves of {\em degree $d$} passing through $3d-1$ points in general position. Then $n_d$ is finite and non-zero.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md: Let $0 \leq k \leq 3d-1$. Let $n_{d,k}$ be the number of {\em rational curves} passing through $k$ points and meeting $(3d-1-k)$ lines tangentially. Then $n_{d,k}$ is finite and non-zero.

title: Theorem
body_md:
For $z \notin P_{\Delta}$, let 
	 
	$${\mathcal Z}_{{\mathcal Q}_0}(z)=(\hat{{\mathcal C}}(z),f_{P(z)}) + (E_{P(z)},g_{P(z)})$$
	 
	Then ${\mathcal Z}_{{\mathcal Q}_0}(z)$ is an element of the group $H^3_{{\mathcal M}}(\hat{K}_{A_z},{\mathds Q}(2))$. Further, it defines an element of the motivic cohomology group of the generic fibre $H^3_{{\mathcal M}}(\hat{K}_{A_{\eta}},{\mathds Q}(2))$ which is {\bf indecomposable} and has boundary  a non-zero multiple of $\hat{{\mathcal C}}_1(z)-\hat{{\mathcal C}}_2(z)$ in the fibres over $P_{\Delta}$, up to the boundary of a decomposable element.

label: univjacobian
title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $D$ be a curve of genus $g$  and $P$ a point on $D$.  Let $\eta: D \rightarrow A$  be a map from $D$ to an Abelian variety $A$ such that $\eta(P)=0$.  Then there is a unique {\bf homomorphism} $\tilde{\eta}:J(D) \longrightarrow A$ such that 
		 
		$$\eta=\tilde{\eta} \circ \iota_P$$
		  
where $\iota_P:D \longrightarrow J(C)$ is the map 
 
$$\iota_P(x)=x-P$$
\label{univjacobian}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(Sketch). Define $\tilde{\eta}:D^g \longrightarrow A$ by 
	 
	$$\tilde{\eta}(Q_1,\dots,Q_g)=\sum \eta(Q_i)$$
	 
	This is clearly invariant under the symmetric group and hence descends to a rational map, which we also call $\tilde{\eta}:J(D) \longrightarrow A$. Further, this can be seen to be a morphism which sends $0$ to $0$ and is hence a homomorphism. The map $\iota_P:D \longrightarrow J(D)$ is the composite of the maps $D \rightarrow D^g \rightarrow J(D)$ given by $Q \rightarrow (Q,P,\dots, P)$ and $(Q_1,\dots,Q_g) \rightarrow \sum_i \iota_P(Q_i)$. Hence $\eta=\tilde{\eta} \circ \iota_P$.
head: environment

label: univjaccor
title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $D$ be a curve of genus $g$ and  $\mu:D \rightarrow A $ be a map such that $\mu(D)=Q$ for some point $Q$ on $A$. Then there is a morphism $\tilde{\mu}:J(C) \rightarrow A$ such that
	 
	$$\mu=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_P$$
	 
	Further, if $P'$ is another point such that $\mu(P')=Q$, then $\mu=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_{P'}$ as well. 
	\label{univjaccor}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\eta=T_{-Q} \circ \mu$ where $T_{*}:A \rightarrow A$ is the translation map $T_*(x)=x+*$. Then $\eta:C \rightarrow A$ satisfies $\eta(P)=0$ and we can apply Proposition  \ref{univjacobian}. Hence there is a homomorphism $\tilde{\eta}:J(C) \rightarrow A$ such that $T_{-Q} \circ \mu=\eta=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_P$. Let $\tilde{\mu}=T_Q \circ \tilde{\eta}$. One then has 
	 
	$$\mu=T_{Q} \circ \eta= T_{Q} \circ \tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_P=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_P$$
	 
	Since the construction of $\tilde{\eta}$ involves only $\eta$ and not $P$ it does not depend on the choice of $P$ in $\mu^{-1}(Q)$.

title: Lemma
body_md: The points lying over the node $P$ under the map $\tilde{{\mathcal D}} \rightarrow {\mathcal D}$ are ramification points of the map $\tilde{\phi}:{\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}\rightarrow \tilde{\mathcal C}$. To reduce notation, we will continue to call them $P_1,P_2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: One has an involution $i$ on $A$ induced by the double cover $\phi:A \rightarrow K_A$ which restricts to give the hyperelliptic involution on ${\mathcal D}$. The point $P$ on ${\mathcal C}$ is fixed by $i$. In the blow up of $K_A$ at $P$  every point in the  exceptional fibre $E_P$ is fixed by $i$ and hence so are the points $P_1$ and $P_2$. Hence they are ramification points of the hyperelliptic curve ${\tilde{{\mathcal D}}} \rightarrow \tilde{\mathcal C}$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $Z_{P_1P_2,R_1}$ be the Collino cycle corresponding to $P_1$ and $P_2$, where $R_1$ is a Weierstrass point mapping to the point $R$ on ${\mathcal D}$. Then 
 
$$\tilde{\mu}_*(Z_{P_1P_2,R'})=2 \Xi_{P,R}$$
 
where $\tilde{\mu}$ is the map $J({\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}) \longrightarrow A$ obtained by  Corollary \ref{univjaccor}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
From Corollary \ref{univjaccor} The map $\mu:{\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}\rightarrow {\mathcal D}$ determines a map $\mu:{\tilde{{\mathcal D}}} \rightarrow A$ which takes $P_1$   to $P$ and detemines a morphism $\tilde{\mu}:J({\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}) \longrightarrow A$ such that 
	$\mu=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_{P_1}$. Under this map the $({\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}_{P_1},f_{P_1})$ is taken to $\Xi_{P,R}$  Howvever, the map also takes $P_2$ to $P$ and one has $\mu=\tilde{\mu} \circ \iota_{P_2}$. Hence it takes $({\tilde{{\mathcal D}}}_{P_2},f_{P_2})$ is also take to $\Xi_{P,R}$ as well. 
	
	\begin{comment}                                                                              
 
                                                                                              
                                                                                                           
                                                                                                            
                                                              
\end{comment}
	 
	So the image of $C_{P_2}$ is the same as $C_{P_1}$. Hence both the cycles which make up $Z_{P_1P_2,R}$ map to the same cycle  $\Xi_{P,R}$ and we have 
	 
	$$\tilde{\mu}_*(Z_{P_1P_2,R})=2 \Xi_{P,R}$$

title: Corollary
body_md: Recall that there is an extension class $\bar{e}^4_{P_1P_2,R}$ in $\operatorname{Ext}_{MHS}({\mathds Z}(-g),H^{2g-2}(J({\tilde{{\mathcal D}}})))$ corresponding to Collino's cycle $Z_{P_1P_2,R_1}$. From the theorem above, the class  $\frac{1}{2}\tilde{\mu}_*(\bar{e}^4_{P_1P_2,R})$  is the extension class corresponding to the cycle $\Xi_{P,R}$ in $\operatorname{Ext}_{MHS}({\mathds Z}(-2),H^2(A))$.
